To make sure this new functionality behaves as intended, I wrote a set of unit tests in `tests/test_stm.py`. The first test checks that `round_config` correctly tightens the floor quantile on each round and increments the seed. The second test verifies that the floor quantile never goes below the specified minimum. The third test ensures that passing an invalid round index (zero) raises a `ValueError`. I ran the test suite, and the output shows all eight tests passed (`8 passed in 1.05s`). That gives me confidence that the core logic for round handling is solid.
